quote.text: You've got to start with the customer experience and work back toward the technology, not the other way around.

term.name: Agentic commerce
term.def: When an AI agent finds, compares and buys things on someone’s behalf. The new question: how do you market to a buyer that is software?

stories.headline: AWS Marketplace now lets AI agents do the buying
stories.summary: AI agents can now purchase select AWS Marketplace products. Buyers set spending limits first, every agent purchase is logged, and an Agent Mode asks a human to confirm. AWS says Agent Mode buyers convert at 6% to 7%, though it didn't share how it measured that.
stories.takeaway: If agents are shopping, your listing, pricing page and docs have to be readable by a machine. Clear, structured product info becomes a marketing asset.

stories.headline: Klarna is the first non-card option in Adyen's agent checkout
stories.summary: Klarna is now inside Adyen Agentic, Adyen's suite for purchases made by AI agents. Shoppers still confirm each purchase, and merchants already using Klarna through Adyen can turn it on with no new integration.
stories.takeaway: "No new integration" is the whole pitch. In B2B, lowering switching effort often sells better than adding features.

stories.headline: Dropbox is buying Tigris Data for $350 million
stories.summary: Dropbox is acquiring Tigris Data to power DBX Agent Cloud, a storage platform for developers building AI models and agents.
stories.takeaway: A consumer-famous brand is repositioning toward developers and AI. Watch how they rewrite their messaging for a brand-new audience.

stories.headline: Base acquires Rubiq to build a "Customer Graph"
stories.summary: Base, an AI customer-growth platform, bought Rubiq, a young company that maps customer context into a knowledge graph. It now powers the Customer Graph in Base's Orbit platform. Base lists Adobe, Okta and ZoomInfo as customers.
stories.takeaway: Notice the named logos. Customer logos are social proof, and B2B buyers look for them before they read anything else.

stories.headline: AI usage keeps climbing while AI spend flattens
stories.summary: Ramp's spending data shows companies using more AI while spending roughly the same, because of price cuts and tighter cost controls among heavy users.
stories.takeaway: When budgets tighten, messaging shifts from "look what it can do" to "look what it saves you." ROI stories win.

stories.headline: Salesforce study: shoppers don't trust agents with their wallet yet
stories.summary: In a survey of 2,500+ holiday shoppers, 22% of AI-agent users had an agent blocked from finishing a purchase, 27% said an agent bought something too expensive, and 73% are uncomfortable giving an agent payment info.
stories.takeaway: Trust is the objection to handle. Vendors in this space will lead with controls, limits and approvals, just like AWS did.

stories.headline: Siteimprove sells its Accessibility Agent to other agents
stories.summary: Siteimprove launched as a partner on AWS's agent marketplace. Other AI agents can pay per request to use its Accessibility Agent. The price per request wasn't shared.
stories.takeaway: Pay-per-request is usage-based pricing. Learn the difference between seat, usage and outcome pricing; it comes up in every PMM interview.

stories.headline: Fast Simon ships an MCP server for developers
stories.summary: Fast Simon, a product discovery platform, released an MCP server that works in AI coding tools like Claude Code and Cursor. Merchants can ask it questions about top searches and widget performance.
stories.takeaway: MCP is how tools plug into AI assistants. Launching "where the user already works" is a classic distribution play.

stories.headline: Mirendil and Mercor raise giant AI rounds
stories.summary: Mirendil raised a $1 billion Series A and Mercor raised $750 million, among the largest rounds of the week, both in AI infrastructure and agentic AI.
stories.takeaway: Big rounds mean those companies will hire and spend on go-to-market soon. Funding news doubles as a job-search lead list.

stories.headline: Clinch adds ByteDance's image and video models for advertisers
stories.summary: Clinch, an ad platform, added ByteDance's Seedream and Seedance models alongside OpenAI and Google. Clients can control which models their teams use and how content is approved.
stories.takeaway: Enterprise buyers care about governance as much as features. "Control who can use what" is a selling point, not a footnote.

sources.name: The Art of CTO SaaS outlook (Nov 16)
